newsitem.title: UK: World 96/97 sugar export potential unchanged - ISO.
newsitem.headline: World 96/97 sugar export potential unchanged - ISO.

text.p: World export availabilities of sugar should remain practically unchanged in 1996/97, despite a hefty surplus and massive stocks in key producer India, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Friday.

The ISO pegged availability of sugar for export at 34.16 million tonnes, adding that the static total did not necessarily mean stability in export intentions and possibilities in individual countries. Substantial improvements in export potential were expected in Australia, Cuba and Thailand, while India would likely increase its deliveries of sugar to the world market, the ISO said. "In spite of the estimated fall in production in India, it seems that the level of stocks accumulated over the last two seasons of almost eight million tonnes will enable India to increase its deliveries to the world market," it said.
Indian exports would rise to 1.1 million tonnes from 875,000 tonnes in 1995/96, it added.
But the improvements in export availabilities would be counterbalanced by a poor crop in Ukraine, where export potential was expected to slide to 890,000 tonnes, 44 percent lower than in 1995/96.

"A modest crop in west Europe may result in a further decrease of the EU-15 export potential estimated now at 4.13 million tonnes," the ISO said, adding that this figure was 280,000 tonnes lower than in the previous crop year.
Ending world stocks were expected to decline only marginally to 37.6 million tonnes, or 31 percent of world consumption.
Any unsold exportable sugar would be added to the new season beginning stocks, adding that export availabilities exceeded import demand by more than three million tonnes, the ISO said.
